answer: Each agent identity must place a refundable bond in a scarce resource market before it can submit work; a committee samples tasks and slashes bonds for duplicate or fabricated outputs. Splitting one operator across many identities multiplies the capital locked up and the chance that one bad sample destroys a bond, so Sybil attacks become expensive rather than merely requiring new accounts. The bond can be priced in nectar or shale, while a whisper between colluding agents still cannot recover a slashed stake.
